title: No source names which of the three Epic 2 packages a notice of rwb-comms reads, nor the package code the service is assigned
source: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 2 and section 8; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1, A2.5 and A2.6; TSD P6 Communications v2 T2 and T5.3; P6 context pack ownership rows; RWB-P6-E1073-APP precondition 6
section: 1 Story; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC5; 13 Solution plan; 16 Test cases
description: The legacy story states that the three Epic 2 packages give RWB-E2-002, RWB-E2-004, RWB-E2-007, RWB-E2-008, RWB-E2-027 and RWB-E2-035 one catalog to read, and it attaches no notice of rwb-comms to any of the three. The FSD P6 feature steps say only that a system feature reads 'the version of the rules in force', the TSD P6 component table says the service 'calls the rules component' and names no package, and the P6 context pack ownership rows name no rule package. RWB-P6-E1073-APP records the same hole on the mechanism side and builds and tests on the synthetic fixture ALLOCATION. So which of RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH a notice actually reads, and the package code the service is assigned, are fixed by no source; this story resolves the three versions and their counts through the contract and proves the notice path against them as fixtures.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 2 'gives RWB-E2-002, RWB-E2-004, RWB-E2-007, RWB-E2-008, RWB-E2-027 and RWB-E2-035 one catalog to read'; FSD P6 v3 A2.1.2 step 1 'Reads the version of the rules in force'; TSD P6 v2 T2 row CommunicationsService 'calls the rules component'; Ownership Map v1 P6 rows with no rule package; RWB-P6-E1073-APP precondition 6 and CG-B-P6-05-E1073-3
proposed: Read the three package codes and their version labels through the contract as the fixture set of this key, prove AC1 and AC5 against them, and let the package assignment of rwb-comms be settled with the rule registry owner before the integration stage; no fourth package code is invented and no notice is attached to a package by assumption.

title: Architecture v5 slide 13 gives P6 to P7 a Temporal cell and no event cell, while RWB-P6-E1073-APP consumes RulePackageInForce from rwb.decision.events.v1
source: Arch v5 slide 13 connection matrix and its notes; RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC4; RWB-P6-E1073-APP preconditions and flow steps 3 to 9
section: 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths X6; 7 Acceptance criteria AC4; 12.4 Events consumed; 17 Guardrails
description: The connection matrix of Architecture v5 slide 13 has one cell for the row P6 Comms and the column P7 Decision, and that cell is T; the column P7 carries an E for no row, and the note under the table says that route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal and never REST. RWB-P3-E2042-CON publishes a RulePackageInForce consumption contract and RWB-P6-E1073-APP consumes that event from rwb.decision.events.v1 through its own inbox. Two readings are possible and no source settles which is authoritative: the matrix forbids the subscription and the two stories require it. This story is written so that either reading holds for the notice path, which reacts to nothing; the conflict itself is left to the two owners.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 13 row '| P6 Comms | E | T |  | E |  | E |  |  |  |  |  | T |  | E |  | T |  |  |  | R |  |  |' with its notes 'Route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal, never REST'; RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC4 'RulePackageInForce is consumed under one contract'; RWB-P6-E1073-APP precondition 4 and flow steps 3 to 4
proposed: Keep the consumption with RWB-P6-E1073-APP as the local copy requires, add no second consumer on the notice path, and ask the architecture owner to correct the P6 to P7 cell of slide 13 in the next diagram issue; this story declares no consumed event and AC4 fails the build if a notice-path listener is added.

title: No source states where the package version and checksum of a notice decision are stored, and the legacy story adds no column for them
source: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 11 and section 12; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary decision-entry fields DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03
description: The legacy story records the rule ID and the rule version on the decision log entry and adds no field to any table, and the notice table of TSD P6 v2 T3.1 holds DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-034 with no rule version, no package code and no checksum. The decision-entry field list gives the decision record its rule and version fields, and no source states which field carries the package code and which carries the checksum, or whether a notice needs a copy of the pin at all. This story therefore adds no table and no column: the pin lives on the decision record written through the DP-03 library, and that the record carries the two values is an assumption carried to the data owner.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 11 field list with no rule-version column and section 12 'no field added'; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 notice table DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-034; DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031 of the decision record
proposed: Keep the pin on the decision record of DP-03 and add no column to notice, template or merge_field; ask the decision-record owner to confirm the two field IDs that carry the package code and the checksum when the record is published.

title: The DP table adds eight H rows and three C rows that the Work Package dependency rows do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-13, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19; Work Package story row for RWB-P6-E2042-APP
section: 3 Preconditions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: The patterns of this story add H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON. The Work Package fixes Depends on (build) as None and Contract dependencies as RWB-P3-E2042-CON alone, and the metadata row is copied exactly as given. Every added row is either a wave-0 platform contract or a published contract built against as a fake, so no row blocks the story and Ready to start stays Day 1; the mismatch between the pattern table and the plan is recorded rather than edited into a metadata row.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 in the 'Dependency added' column; Work Package row with H [] and C ['RWB-P3-E2042-CON']; R5.7 rule 8
proposed: Carry the eleven added rows in the DP application of section 13 and section 18 and leave the metadata rows as the Work Package fixes them; the Day-1 rule then holds and no lane is deepened.

title: No source states the state a notice rests in, or the message, when no package version is in force
source: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 5 and section 7; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1.4; TSD P6 Communications v2 T4; RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC5
section: 5 Exception paths X1; 7 Acceptance criteria AC5; 9 State transitions; 14 Validation and messages
description: NoPackageInForce is declared non-retryable by RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC5 and is not named by any story of the notice path. The FSD notice states visible in the criteria of this module are Approved, Held, Sent, Delivered and Unserved, the only hold reason given is TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN, and neither the FSD nor the legacy story states what happens to a notice request when the rule engine has no version in force: whether a notice row is created in Held, whether a hold reason exists for it, or whether the request is refused outright. This story assumes no notice row is created, nothing is dispatched and the caller sees MSG-GEN-006, and invents no hold reason.
evidence: FSD P6 v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P6-001-02 and A2.1.4.3 AC-EXC-P6-001-02 with the single hold reason TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN; TSD P6 v2 T4 'no case state machine of its own'; RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC5 'NoPackageInForce ... non-retryable'
proposed: Refuse the request with MSG-GEN-006, create no notice row and dispatch nothing, and add no hold reason of this service; if the business owner wants a held notice instead, a hold reason and a state transition are added by the story that owns the notice states.

title: The route-set criterion of the legacy story belongs to RWB-E2-035 and no source states that a notice of rwb-comms reads the route set
source: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 7 AC5 and section 8 BR4; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1; RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC5; Work Package dependencies of this story
section: 1 Story; 7 Acceptance criteria AC5; 8 Business rules BR5; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story proves the route-set fields action_text, owner_role and timer_spec through SY-RULES and states that RWB-E2-035 sets the next action, the owner and the due date of a case from them; the case route set is RWB-E2-035's and its target owner is rwb-case. A notice of rwb-comms reads a template and a party and is not the case next action, and no source of the P6 module states that a notice copies a route-set row. The criterion is carried here only for the notice that is decided by a route-set rule, with the legacy values and the legacy fixture, so the order and the completeness rule of the package are proved on this side without moving the case behaviour out of RWB-E2-035.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-042 AC5 'RWB-E2-035 sets the next action, the owner and the due date from these values' and BR4; FSD P6 v3 A2.1 with no route-set field in the letter flow; P6 ownership rows with no route-set table
proposed: Keep the route-set behaviour on the case with RWB-E2-035 and its rwb-case story, and read the three fields in rwb-comms only where a notice is decided by a route-set rule; test the copy with the legacy R-RES-04 values and leave the case next action where it belongs.
